TCP/IP was designed for the US Department of Defense (DoD) to keep data accurate and communications working even after serious damage to the network. TCP appeared in 1973. In 1978 it was split into two protocols,

. In 1983 TCP/IP replaced the older NCP and became the official transport for ARPAnet, the ancestor of the Internet. Much of the development work happened at UC Berkeley, where TCP/IP was bundled into BSD Unix and passed to other universities. The open, standards-based approach is a big reason it won.
For the exam, you only need the idea: TCP/IP is an open standard from the DoD era, so any vendor's hardware and software can use it.
